chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Mu'az told us, saying: Al-Husayn al-Marwazi told us, saying: Abdullah told us, saying: Ibn 'Awn told us, from Al-Hasan, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

God the Blessed the Exalted said: By My Honor and My Grandeur, I do not combine for My servant two fears and two securities. If I make him secure in the world, I will frighten him on the Day of Resurrection, and if he fears Me in the world, I will make him secure on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between fear of God in this world and security on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith qudsi establishes a divine principle of reciprocal balance where worldly spiritual posture determines the afterlife state. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *khawf* (fear of God) as a protective shield against the greater terror of the Hereafter, contrasting worldly complacency with eschatological anxiety. This reciprocal dynamic serves as a practical motivation for maintaining constant vigilance (*muraqabah*) in daily worship.
